summary: Colombia admits holders of the passports on its Foreign Ministry's List A — including the US, UK, EU, Canada and many countries of the Americas — without a visa for short stays; the UK government's travel advice gives the stay as up to 90 days, and Migración Colombia allows an extension up to a maximum of 180 days per calendar year. Nationalities that do need a visa apply for a Visitor (V) visa through the Foreign Ministry. Migración Colombia's free Check-Mig pre-registration, before entering or leaving, is optional and speeds up the immigration interview.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says pickpocketing, mugging and armed robbery are a problem in the major cities, including Bogotá, Medellín, Cali and the Caribbean coast, and criminals use drugs such as scopolamine to rob victims, as well as dating apps to lure lone travellers; express kidnappings happen in unlicensed taxis, so use licensed phone or app taxis. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of the country, including all of Norte de Santander and Arauca, much of the Pacific coast and Chocó, Guaviare, parts of Caquetá, Meta, Cauca and Putumayo, and areas near the Venezuelan and Ecuadorian borders.

The UK Foreign Office reports express kidnappings, assaults and robberies in unlicensed taxis and advises using licensed telephone or internet-based taxi services, or booking through your hotel; at Bogotá's El Dorado airport only authorised taxis may pick up passengers.

Canada's travel advice says Bogotá lies at 2,600 m above sea level and that high-altitude illness is possible in parts of the country. The UK Foreign Office says tap water is safe to drink only in Bogotá, and advises drinking only bottled water and avoiding ice in drinks.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Colombia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days, extendable in-country to a maximum of 180 days per calendar year. They must hold an onward ticket; the free Check-Mig pre-registration is optional.

faq.question: What is Check-Mig and is it really free?
faq.answer: Check-Mig is Migración Colombia's optional online pre-registration, submitted between 72 hours and 1 hour before an international trip into or out of Colombia to speed up the immigration interview. Migración Colombia says the service is completely free.

faq.question: How can I stay in Colombia longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: At least 5 business days before your entry permit expires, apply online to Migración Colombia for a Permiso Temporal de Permanencia extension of up to 90 more days. Visa-free visitors cannot exceed 180 calendar days in the same calendar year.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Colombia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from certain countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission, when you must show a vaccination certificate. The UK Foreign Office says you may also be asked to show it if you are travelling to areas of Colombia considered high risk, so carry the certificate at all times.

faq.question: Do Indian or Chinese citizens need a visa for Colombia?
faq.answer: Yes, unless they qualify under Colombia's List C of conditional exemptions: Indian and Chinese holders of a US or Schengen visa valid for more than 180 days on the day they enter need no visa for a short stay. Others apply for a Visitor (V) visa through the Cancillería.
